lines.text: Noise-cancelling headphones make a jet engine fade away. The trick? They add more sound, not less.
A tiny microphone on the outside of each ear cup listens to the noise around you.
A chip makes a copy of that sound wave, flipped upside down, and plays it through the speaker.
Where a peak meets a valley, they cancel. Two sounds add up to almost nothing.
A second mic inside the cup hears what still leaks through, and keeps correcting.
It works best on low, steady sounds like engine hum, because they repeat and are easy to predict.
Voices and sudden sounds change too fast, so the soft cushions have to block those instead.
The idea goes back to the 1950s, to quiet helicopter and airplane cockpits.
